title: Measuring Output Diversity Within a Single Model Across Deployment Contexts (System Prompt Variation)

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if system prompt variation produces more diversity than multiple models, this is an immediately actionable finding. Directly useful for deployment guidance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Highly accessible: query one model with different system prompts via API, compute output similarity. No ML training or complex setup required. Perfect for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one model, 20 system prompts, fixed query set, compare to inter-model baseline. Clear experimental design completable well within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: While prompt engineering effects on output diversity have been studied (e.g., structured prompts reducing diversity), no existing work directly compares system-prompt-induced intra-model diversity against inter-model diversity as a baseline. The specific question 'can deployment context variation within one model match or exceed the diversity you get from multiple models?' is novel and practically important.

evidence.source: The Price of Format: Diversity Collapse in LLMs (2025)
evidence.finding: Shows that structured prompts consistently yield lower semantic and topical diversity than simple prompts, even under high-temperature decoding—suggesting format constrains diversity more than randomness.
Measures inter-model homogeneity extensively but does not compare intra-model diversity under system prompt variation against the inter-model baseline.
